description: B'Tselem found the forbidden roads regime has never been set out in Knesset legislation, political decisions, military orders, press releases or even road signs. It runs on verbal orders to soldiers and on practice.
energy_note: A law you can be punished under and never read.

description: Completely prohibited roads, for Israeli vehicles only, including what the army calls 'sterile roads' with a checkpoint that passes Israeli vehicles only; partially prohibited roads needing a Civil Administration permit; and restricted-use roads, nominally open but blocked with concrete.
energy_note: Open, permitted, or blocked with a concrete cube.

aspect: Roughly 105km barred outright by plate colour
description: B'Tselem found Palestinian-plated vehicles completely barred from about 105km of West Bank roads. The driver's documents are irrelevant; the plate decides.
energy_note: Your car is the wrong nationality.

aspect: The planning vocabulary says it plainly
description: Israeli planning distinguishes 'fabric of life' roads, which divert Palestinian traffic away from settlers, from 'bypass' roads, which divert settlers away from Palestinian towns. Both exist to keep the two apart; only one is built to a good standard.
energy_note: Two road networks, one country, one of them resurfaced.

description: A road near Jerusalem with a concrete wall down the middle: one side for Israeli vehicles, the other for Palestinian traffic. It became the emblem because it makes the arrangement literally visible.
energy_note: A wall down the centre line of a road.

aspect: Being forced onto back roads has a compounding cost
description: Poorly maintained secondary routes mean longer journeys, more fuel, more vehicle wear, more accidents and more exposure to the villages where settler violence happens.
money_note: Annual fuel, wear and repair premium.
energy_note: A worse road, and more of it.

aspect: It fragments the territory, which is the point
description: The network is arranged so that Palestinian areas connect to each other badly and settlements connect to Israel well. The daily cost is time; the structural effect is that the places do not join up.
energy_note: A map designed so the pieces don't touch.

aspect: EXAMPLE - Route 443, and the one time a court intervened
description: In 2009 Israel's Supreme Court issued a first-of-its-kind ruling ordering the army to reopen a West Bank highway to Palestinian traffic. It concerned Route 443, where obstacles on both sides prevented Palestinians from driving to and from nearby villages. One road, one ruling, in two decades of the regime.
energy_note: One highway, reopened by a court, once.

aspect: EXAMPLE - October 2005, the temporary measure that stayed
description: Israel barred private Palestinian vehicles from several West Bank highways in October 2005, expanding a network of settler-only routes after a drive-by shooting killed three settlers. The army billed the restrictions as temporary security measures; a plan was then considered to permanently designate roads for separate use.
energy_note: Announced as temporary in 2005, still in force.
